# Scene historical evidence synthesis — task01, batch 1 of 1

## Coverage and evidence matrix

The supplied inventory and full-observation audit reports cover all **8 files** in this group, each with 12 JSONL lines. These are file counts, not counts of independent trials: the paths repeat two example IDs across four conditions. The reports, rather than raw images or source files, are the basis of this synthesis. In the path column, every entry is relative to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_4/results/task01/` and ends in `/trajectory.jsonl`.

| Source and relative path | Observed attempt and outcome | Key evidence |
|---|---|---|
| S0258 `structured/C1/test/commons_192968130` | Kitchen interpretation; revised camera, cabinets, sink, materials and lighting. Both renders ran and were selected; quality unknown. | Lines 3–7, 9–12 |
| S0259 `structured/C1/selection/commons_31294395` | Bedroom interpretation; revised chair, bed, screen, camera and appearance. Both builds ran and were selected; quality unknown. | Lines 3–7, 9–12 |
| S0260 `fixed/C1/test/commons_192968130` | Kitchen interpretation; revised door, sink, cupboards, material assignment and lighting. Both builds ran and were selected; quality unknown. | Lines 3–7, 9–12 |
| S0261 `fixed/C1/selection/commons_31294395` | Bedroom interpretation; revised architecture, bed, chair, materials and lighting, retaining the camera. Both builds ran and were selected; quality unknown. | Lines 3–7, 9–12 |
| S0262 `reference/H_start/test/commons_192968130` | Kitchen interpretation; revised camera, layout, cabinets, lighting and bounds-based material assignment. Both builds ran and were selected; quality unknown. | Lines 3–7, 9–12 |
| S0263 `reference/H_start/selection/commons_31294395` | Bedroom interpretation; revised chair, bed, camera, lighting and wallpaper. Both builds ran and were selected; quality unknown. | Lines 3–7, 9–12 |
| S0264 `active/C1/test/commons_192968130` | Kitchen interpretation; revised camera, layout, sink, cabinetry, materials and lighting. Both builds ran and were selected; quality unknown. | Lines 3–7, 9–12 |
| S0265 `active/C1/selection/commons_31294395` | Bedroom interpretation; revised bed, chair, screen, camera, lighting and wallpaper. Both builds ran and were selected; quality unknown. | Lines 3–7, 9–12 |

## Comparative findings

All eight visible trajectories contain an initial scene build followed by a substantive, executed revision after the student received a first render for comparison. Both executions in each file reported success and were selected. The revisions were **not empty patches**. Those observations establish technical execution and selection, not successful photographic reconstruction or a formal acceptance judgment. No subsequent independent visual review or formal score is visible. The reference photographs and renders cannot be inspected from the supplied reports, so even partial visual correctness is unknown.

There is no documented failed or interrupted attempt, permission or branch stop, or CLI stop in these eight traces. The recorded student CLI sessions report zero tool calls; that is not a failed CLI operation and does not negate the separate runner executions. Nor is there a demonstrated algorithmic failure: a student's diagnosis of a problem and its attempted correction are different from an independently verified failure or fix. These absences characterize this batch only, not all Scene work.

The two recurring example IDs are also counterexamples to treating the four condition paths as interchangeable results. For the kitchen interpretation, S0258 changed camera position and alignment, whereas S0260 retained the camera while changing other scene elements (each lines 9–10). For the bedroom interpretation, S0261 retained the camera while S0263 changed its position and aim (each lines 9–10). Both alternatives executed, but the reports do not establish which, if either, better matched the photograph. Condition labels and repeated example IDs do not establish independent trials or causal superiority.

## Advice, diagnosis and adoption

No separate teacher message, teacher diagnosis, proposed teacher update, or receipt and adoption of one is visible in any of the eight student trajectories. This is a limit on the observed record, not proof that no advice existed elsewhere. Runner-provided comparison instructions and the first render were available to and received by the students—for example, S0264 lines 5–7 and S0265 lines 6–7—but are not identified as teacher intervention.

Students did make diagnoses and execute updates. S0262 attributed a material-selection problem to generic primitive names and executed bounds-based selection (lines 9–10); S0265 similarly attributed missing wallpaper to naming and changed assignment (lines 7–10). These are observed student claims and actions, not independently established diagnoses or successful fixes. Likewise, selection after execution is visible; acceptance of visual quality is not. The audit cannot infer a teacher's detection, advice effectiveness, or adoption from autonomous revision.

## Transferable constraints and unresolved hypotheses

- **Execution and semantic structure are not visual or geometric validation.** Named objects and children show intended organization, but not correct contact, support, occlusion or resemblance. S0258's revised sink includes a Boolean opening and separate basin parts, yet their fit is unverified (lines 9–12); S0264's layered-box sink likewise does not establish an opening or support (lines 3–4).
- **Coupled changes limit attribution.** S0258 changed camera, geometry and lighting together; S0265 changed camera, furniture, materials and lighting (each lines 9–10). Even an observed later improvement would not isolate an individual change's effect from these traces.
- **Task-specific observations remain hypotheses.** The kitchen and bedroom inventories are student interpretations, not independently verified photograph contents. S0261 explicitly considered camera versus local geometry as competing explanations (lines 7–10); S0260's nearest-center material assignment and S0262's bounds-based assignment were executed but not visually validated (each lines 9–12). Grouped parts and coordinated transforms are evidenced, for example in S0259 lines 3–4 and 9–10, but do not prove correct pose or physical connections.

Missing formal scores remain **unknown**, not zero. No old model cost can be recovered from its absence. This synthesis is audit-only and does not supply new solutions, skills or test feedback.
